description:
Track time worked against threads, billable or not, stored one file per thread under hours/.

Subcommands:
  log [THREAD] [DESCRIPTION...] [-m MINUTES] [-r RATE] [-c CURRENCY] [-d DATE] [-t TIME] [--all] — append an entry; INTERACTIVE if THREAD is omitted
  list [THREAD] [--since DATE] [--until DATE] [--json] — list entries
  report [--thread T] [--since DATE] [--until DATE] [--json] — totals by thread and currency, unbilled time totalled separately
  show ID [--json] — show one entry
  edit ID [--description TEXT] [-m MINUTES] [-r RATE] [-c CURRENCY] [-d DATE] [-t TIME] — change fields of an entry
  rm ID [-y] — delete an entry

Flags:
  log: -m duration in minutes, default 60; -r hourly rate, 0 means unbillable; -c 3-letter ISO currency, defaults to the thread's, and with neither the entry is recorded as unbilled; -d date YYYY-MM-DD, default today; -t time HH:MM, default now; --all only affects the interactive picker
  list: --since, --until inclusive YYYY-MM-DD bounds; --json
  report: --thread limit to one thread; --since, --until; --json
  show: --json
  edit: --description new description text; -m, -r, -c, -d, -t as for log
  rm: -y skip confirmation

Examples:
  ["log", "Projects/SGB", "Drafted the integration spec", "-m", "90"]
  ["list", "Projects/SGB", "--since", "2026-08-01", "--json"]
  ["report", "--since", "2026-08-01", "--until", "2026-08-31", "--json"]
  ["rm", "a1b2c3d4", "-y"]

Notes:
  Never call `log` without THREAD — it falls into an interactive picker reading stdin. Always pass the thread and description as arguments.
  Multi-word descriptions may be passed as several trailing elements or as one quoted element; the description is the invoice line item.
  THREAD accepts a bare thread name, 'Kind/Name', or a wikilink.
  ID is the 8-hex-char entry id shown by `list`; ids share one namespace with `payments`.
  Rate and currency are resolved at write time and stored on the entry, so changing the thread's defaults never re-prices history. Asking for a rate with no currency is refused.
  `rm` prompts for confirmation unless -y is given.
